C-0001.text: SUPERSEDED — replaced by C-0001-REV (EV-0030). Original (disputed): reliable, replicable network changes. Revised: direction-consistent but HETEROGENEOUS; posterior regions most reliable; DLPFC three-signature pattern rests mainly on Stanford/Spiegel lab and not cleanly independently replicated.
C-0001.verifier_notes: cycle 2: superseded by C-0001-REV (EV-0030). Original framing 'reliable, replicable' was disputed in cycle 1; revised claim addresses the dispute. C-0001-REV now consistent with C-0002 (no contradiction).

C-0001-REV.text: Hypnosis produces DIRECTION-CONSISTENT but HETEROGENEOUS changes in large-scale network connectivity. Posterior regions (precuneus/cuneus/lingual) most reliably implicated across independent groups; the DLPFC-centric 'three-signature' pattern rests substantially on one lab (Stanford/Spiegel) and is not cleanly independently replicated.
C-0001-REV.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 2: verified. ALE meta-analysis (EV-0028 Landry 2017) confirms lingual gyrus is the only consistent ALE peak; EV-0029 (provenance) confirms DLPFC three-signature pattern is mainly Spiegel-lab, partially (not cleanly) converged on by de Matos/Vazquez. Posterior-region reliability well-supported.

C-0006.text: 2023-2024 meta-analytic evidence supports REAL but MODEST clinical efficacy of hypnosis, especially for pain and procedural anxiety; effects heterogeneous and certainty low-to-very-low; over active psychological controls the added benefit is small or absent.
C-0006.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 2: verified. EV-0024 (Akkermann 2024 meta-review, 49 meta-analyses/261 RCTs) and EV-0025 (adjunctive pain meta-analysis n=6078) directly support real-but-modest efficacy, heterogeneity, low certainty, small/no benefit over active psychological controls.

C-0007.text: The predictive-coding/active-inference unifying framework is theoretically appealing but its HYPNOSIS-SPECIFIC predictions have NOT been decisively empirically tested; foundational PC/AI evidence is only 'modest' and alternative feedforward models explain similar results.
C-0007.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 2: verified. EV-0026 (Pean 2023 foundational review: PC 'modest support,' AI not validated vs alternatives) and EV-0027 (Lush/Dienes/Seth: Martin&Pacherie model falsifiable but anomalies, predictions not decisively tested) directly support the claim that hypnosis-PC predictions are not yet decisively tested.

C-0008.text: The decisive hypnosis-vs-expectancy/placebo test yields MIXED evidence: sham/expectancy-matched controls account for a LARGE fraction (~80% in hot-flash RCT) of the effect, and formal induction often produces no reliable EEG change — but a small hypnosis-specific residual persists. This is the field's central unresolved empirical question.
C-0008.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 3: verified. EV-0033 (Elkins 2025 sham RCT n=250: 53.4% vs 40.9%, sham ~80% of effect), EV-0034 (2023 EEG n=31: induction no spectral changes), EV-0035 (2024 n=47: expectations not associated with outcome). The mixed pattern is honestly reported; verifier confirms the three EVs together support the 'mixed/central-unresolved' framing rather than cherry-picking one side.

C-0002.text: There is NO single, replicable, unique 'hypnosis signature' in the brain — effects are heterogeneous across studies, suggestions, and individuals; the ALE meta-analysis linked hypnosis to lingual gyrus, not the hypothesized DMN/SN/ECN.
C-0002.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 1: verified. EV-0001, EV-0004 (ALE meta-analysis → lingual gyrus not DMN/SN/ECN), EV-0007 (no single mechanism; aperiodic slope = best baseline predictor), EV-0014 (highly heterogeneous) all support.

C-0003.text: The state vs non-state dichotomy is increasingly considered a false one; 2023-2024 work (predictive coding, SATH, response-set-with-PC) shows both positions can be computationally reconciled within a unified framework.
C-0003.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 1: verified. Six independent 2023-2024 sources (EV-0009/0010/0011/0012/0015/0016) converge on predictive-coding/integrative reconciliation and Jensen's 'redirect away from state/nonstate contrast.'

C-0004.text: Pure social-compliance/role-playing is empirically insufficient — surreptitious-observation and simulator studies show genuine high-hypnotizable behavior persists without observation and shows involuntariness/trance-logic that simulators don't reproduce.
C-0004.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 1: verified. EV-0017 (surreptitious observation, primary) is load-bearing; EV-0008/0013 (non-state theorists concede real brain changes). EV-0018 (Spanos) qualifies but does not contradict the core claim that PURE compliance is insufficient.

C-0005.text: Sociocognitive factors (expectancy, context, demand) demonstrably modulate hypnotic responding, and induction effects are often small relative to non-hypnotic suggestibility — social factors are real, significant contributors.
C-0005.verifier_notes: verifier-facts cycle 1: verified. EV-0010 (r=0.67/0.82; induction effects often small), EV-0008 (expectancy intensifies suggestion), EV-0018 (Spanos), EV-0013 (sociocognitive core) all support.
